items.headline: Trump calls GDP data 'fake,' demands Commerce probe
items.summary: President Trump accused the Commerce Department of deliberately releasing inaccurate growth figures before the midterms, after third-quarter GDP was revised up to a 4.3% annual rate from 3.4%. He called it a "massive, and purposeful, error" and said he wants an investigation.

items.headline: Thanksgiving storms knock out power to nearly 1 million
items.summary: Power outages peaked above 980,000 customers across New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and other states as storms stretched from Maine to Florida. More than 400 flights were canceled, and 65 mph gusts tore the roof off a building in Ocean City, Maryland.

items.headline: Zelenskyy warns of imminent Russian strike on power grid
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said intelligence shows Moscow is completing preparations for a new massive strike on Ukraine's energy system, after an overnight barrage of ballistic missiles and 113 drones. U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said peace talks are at "a little bit of a deadlock" over territory.

items.headline: Kim Jong Un vows to expand North Korea's nuclear arsenal
items.summary: State media said Kim inspected two nuclear-material production factories and pledged to build more weapons, citing threats from the U.S. and South Korea. Pyongyang never publicly answered President Trump's offer to meet during his Asia trip.

items.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 cases
items.summary: Ebola is spreading rapidly in eastern Congo, where confirmed cases have passed 12,000 in an outbreak caused by a strain with no approved vaccine. Renewed fighting between rebels and the army is hampering containment and has forced some responders to evacuate.

items.headline: Advocates ask Supreme Court to restore asylum access
items.summary: The administration has blocked asylum claims at the southern border for nearly two years, and the Supreme Court is set to consider whether a president can suspend asylum without Congress. The national asylum denial rate reached 94% in June, up from about 50% in 2024.

items.headline: China, Brazil and EU push back on new U.S. tariff plan
items.summary: China, facing a proposed 20% tariff, said it reserves the right to take necessary measures, and Brazil called the U.S. move "unacceptable." The European Parliament's trade committee chair called the planned 20% rate on EU goods "absurd."

items.headline: Democrats' midterm wins cool the redistricting fight
items.summary: Democrats won several districts in Texas, North Carolina, Ohio, Alabama and Florida that had been redrawn to favor Republicans. Experts say the urgency for more mid-decade redistricting has faded ahead of the next full cycle after the 2030 census.

items.headline: Puerto Rico court lets governor end LUMA grid contract
items.summary: Puerto Rico's Supreme Court cleared the governor to end the contract of LUMA Energy, the company that runs the island's troubled power grid. The government has a year to find a new operator.

items.headline: King tides increasingly flood U.S. coastal towns
items.summary: The year's highest tides are flooding coastal communities more often as sea levels rise, and this year's strong El Niño has pushed water levels higher. Four California locations recorded all-time-high water levels in late October.

digest.overview:
President Trump called new GDP figures "fake" and demanded an investigation of the Commerce Department after third-quarter growth was revised up to 4.3%. Thanksgiving storms knocked out power to more than 980,000 customers at their peak and canceled over 400 flights. Advocates are asking the Supreme Court to restore asylum access after nearly two years of border restrictions. A federal judge declined to extend a block on taxpayer-funded pro-Trump TV ads, saying the midterms had come and gone. Puerto Rico's Supreme Court let the governor end LUMA Energy's contract to run the island's power grid. The EPA said it found zero airborne lead in Middletown, Iowa, after the Army's detonation. Trump will attend a Dec. 4 groundbreaking for TSMC's next Arizona chip plant. Former Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott died at 80.

Abroad, a drone attack on a Kuwaiti air-defense site killed two Italian contractors, and Iran denied responsibility. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines near the Strait of Hormuz, and the Houthis struck Saudi Arabia's Jazan oil complex. Zelenskyy warned of an imminent massive Russian strike on Ukraine's grid, while Ukraine said it damaged five warplanes at Russia's Savasleyka air base. EU leaders failed to agree on a long-term budget and a new loan for Ukraine. Kim Jong Un vowed to expand North Korea's nuclear arsenal, and North Korean troops have crossed the inter-Korean military demarcation line about 40 times since October. Israeli strikes in Gaza killed at least 10 people, including the territory's deputy education minister. Congo's Ebola outbreak passed 12,000 cases.

home.overview:
Philadelphia rallied from 21 points down, the biggest comeback in Thanksgiving Day history, to beat Dallas 39–38 on Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal with three seconds left. Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a touchdown with three seconds to go as the Bears edged the Lions 39–35 for a sixth straight win and sole possession of the NFC North at 9–2, and Tyler Bass's walk-off 57-yarder lifted Buffalo past Kansas City 13–10 to 10–1. The NBA returns tonight with 11 NBA Cup games to close group play; LeBron James became the oldest player to post a triple-double on Wednesday. Baseball's labor deal expires Dec. 1, with talks tentatively set to resume in Phoenix.

Ten-man Bournemouth came from behind to win 2–1 at Celta and stay perfect in the Europa League, Viktoria Plzeň routed Benfica 4–0 and Crystal Palace beat Real Sociedad 2–1, while Monaco stayed perfect in the Conference League with a 3–2 win at Hearts. The Premier League resumes tonight with Forest–Chelsea before Sunday's Merseyside derby and Arsenal–Man City, while Dortmund host Leverkusen and Barcelona visit Deportivo. K League 1 champions FC Seoul host Daejeon this weekend as Ulsan HD defend second place. In the KBO, Korean Series MVP Koo Ja-wook says he is excited about a possible move to MLB.

brief: Samsung's Koo Ja-wook, the Korean Series MVP and a first-time free agent, said he is excited about a possible MLB move and talks with his U.S. agent every day.

Koo collected trophies for leading the KBO in batting average (.371) and on-base percentage (.458) at Thursday's awards ceremony and apologized to Lions fans after introducing himself without naming a team.
MLB has made a formal status check on Koo, though a lockout widely expected after Dec. 1 would halt MLB free-agent negotiations.
MVP Kim Do-yeong also won his first KBO Fielding Award at third base and will move to shortstop in 2027.

brief: MLB and the players' union are tentatively set to resume face-to-face talks Sunday or Monday in Phoenix, with the labor deal expiring at 11:59 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Dec. 1.

Rob Manfred has said a lockout decision will come 'at the last possible moment,' after MLB's Nov. 24 offer to guarantee contracts without escrow in exchange for a salary cap, floor and 50-50 revenue split was condemned by the union.
After Manfred said he is 'not that big on Thanksgiving as a holiday,' the union posted 'Happy Thanksgiving to all those who are big on the holiday!'

fact.answer:
Pruny fingertips aren't simply waterlogged. Soaking triggers an involuntary nervous-system response in which nerve fibers in the fingers tighten the blood vessels beneath the skin. With less blood filling the tissue, the skin loses volume and pulls down into wrinkles. One leading idea is that water entering the sweat glands upsets the skin's salt balance.

For centuries people assumed skin just soaked up water. Studies from the 1930s onward undercut that idea: when the nerves supplying the hand were damaged, fingers didn't wrinkle after soaking.

The wrinkles may work like tire treads, channeling water away so you can grip wet objects with less force, though studies disagree. They take about five minutes to appear, so a long bath or swim, not a quick hand wash, brings them out.
fact.question: Why do your fingers wrinkle in water?
